sources.citation: Head, June. 2011 [created 1976]. A grammar of Umbu-Ungu. Ukarumpa: SIL-PNG manuscript, vi+249 pp. SIL Language & Culture Archives item 42774 (https://www.sil.org/resources/archives/42774); PDF via Wayback 20231208 capture of the SIL reapdata file.
sources.quote: p. 3: 'Stress is also phonemic, but is only written (as an accent over the stressed vowel) to differentiate otherwise identical forms.' p. 16: '5. There is also a pattern in the stress which occurs on verbs ... 5a. For distant past tense and both present tenses stress always falls on the tense marker. 5b. For near past tense and all imperatives stress always falls on the final syllable of the stem. The one exception to this is that for second singular emphatic imperative the stress falls on the first syllable of the stem. 5c. For future tense, customary aspect and subjunctive mood stress alway
sources.locator: ch. 2 sec. 2.1 p. 3 (PDF p. 11); ch. 4 sec. 4.3.4 note 5 p. 16 (PDF p. 24); ch. 4 pronouns p. 23 (PDF p. 31); ch. 3 sec. 3.3 (PDF p. 17)
sources.note: Glottolog's only full grammar (249 pp) by the linguist who checked the OPD; our coding rested on a 4-page OPD sheet. fetched sources now: confirms phonemic stress and spells out the tense-conditioned verb-stress pattern the OPD/Blowers only allude to.
